chunks: Unlawful to you (for marriage) are your mothers and daughters and your sisters and your father's sisters and your mother's sisters and your brother's daughters and your sister's daughters and your mothers who nursed you and your sisters through nursing and the mothers of your wives and your step-daughters under your guardianship born of your wives unto whom you have gone in — but if you have not gone in unto them, there is no blame — and the wives of your sons who are from your own loins, and that you take (in marriage) two sisters simultaneously, except for what has already occurred; indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.

key_terms.إِلَّا مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ: Except for what has already occurred

ai.seo_question: Who are the permanently forbidden wives (Mahram) for men in Islam according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this verse establishes the foundational categories of *Mahram* (permanently forbidden) women, with particular scholarly emphasis on the distinction between *Radāʿah* (milk kinship) and blood ties, as well as the condition of actual consummation (*Dukhūl*) for step-daughters. The prohibition of marrying two sisters simultaneously is interpreted not merely as a restriction but as a preservation of familial harmony, reflecting the divine attribute of *Ghafūran Raḥīm* (All-Forgiving, All-Mercy) which contextualizes the transition from pre-Islamic customs to structured Islamic law.
